title: Change the experiment interface to expose dormant syndrome directions
statement: Uniform private{I,X1,X2,X3} between the known repetition encoder and the unknown iid-bitflip/fixed-mixer channel keeps the same logical identification while giving rho_cal=I8/8, gamma_X=1/8 and gamma_Z=t(1+t^2)/16. It removes the native small-p rare-syndrome penalty at this port, but can worsen the signed gap near p=1/2. Injection is turned OFF for the payload.

One actual ordinary product preparation/readout bank, retained confidence event, finite rational signs and a paid coherent colored decoder
For the injection corollary only: a real known-encoder PRE-noise physical-X port, iid identical bit flips p<=1/2 and a fixed unknown output mixer
provides: A concrete changed-port excitation construction with complete coherent channel identity

Not a universal noise-model-preserving exploration method
costs: All coarse/fine banks and abstained calls; supplied caps, physical traffic, matrices/reflections, routing and implementation budgets

body: Structural fixed Pauli/gauge algebra, locality, current nonanticipation and qualitative contrasts remain promises, not discovered model membership. Calibration may abstain within its funded cap; accepted risk is unnormalized and posterior conditioning needs its denominator. Completion premises concern the declared calibration occupation and transfer observable events, not an arbitrary imperfect occupation. The injection port is genuinely extra access and may violate the class for other correctable sources. The pilot uses one fixed mixer and stationary iid bit flips, not arbitrary retained-memory dynamics or certified rational gate control. Read the exact supporting statement and its applicable conditions. Producer review status is preserved; no new scientific audit or producer-code execution was performed for this insertion.

review.scope: Acquired completed main/theorem, changed-port corollary and floating-pilot reviews at their separate actual versions/scopes. Old candidate headers remain historical; no new scientific audit.
